extracted.intended_audience: Authors and referees for MAA Convergence (teachers of mathematics grades 8–16; math historians; math educators)
extracted.subtask_description: Submission and refereeing guidelines for Convergence (MAA) — a journal publishing history-of-mathematics pieces tied to classroom use for grades 8–16. Covers article types, required pedagogical connection, formats, applet/image requirements, and Mathematical Treasures specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Convergence publishes articles about the history of mathematics and its use in teaching. It is aimed at teachers of mathematics at both the secondary and collegiate levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference is given to topics from grades 8–16 mathematics, with special emphasis on topics from grades 8–14: algebra, combinatorics, synthetic and analytic geometry, trigonometry, probability and statistics, elementary functions, calculus, differential equations, and linear algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical connection requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Convergence articles must address how the history discussed in an article has been—or could be—employed in a mathematics classroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For examples of how these classroom connections can be made, see the tip sheet 'Connecting History to the Mathematics Classroom.' Authors are invited to share how they are using history in their classroom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom activities / modules criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Classroom activities, projects, or modules may be designed for a few minutes, days, or weeks of instruction in grades 8–16 classes and should show how to use history in teaching a particular topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should give potential users as much direction as possible: in which courses; to introduce, develop, and/or review a topic; to replace or supplement traditional instruction; in class and/or homework; estimated time for each; and whether individual or group work. Such pieces may also serve as companion materials to other articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expository article expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Expository articles should address historical topics in the grades 8–16 curriculum and include ideas for classroom use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally include interactive components, animations, colorful graphics, and/or links that take advantage of the online setting. Math historians are encouraged to emphasize classroom suggestions; math educators may present research on the role of history or history-based instructional materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom testimonials
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimonials should describe experiences using a particular teaching aid, article, book, or website in the classroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They may range from informal to formal evaluation, and the outcome may be adoption, adaption, or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations of primary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Translations of primary sources must be accompanied by commentary explaining the work and its context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentary should show Convergence readers how mathematical ideas were developed in various cultures and how knowledge of these developments can be used in teaching the same ideas to today's students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other feature types (brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: Convergence accepts additional short features such as 'Mathematical Treasures', 'Problems from Another Time', 'On This Day', 'Today's Quotation', and the 'Calendar'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each feature has its own focus: e.g., Mathematical Treasures highlights images of important books/manuscripts/objects; Problems from Another Time highlights historical problems; On This Day lists historic mathematical events; Today's Quotation is a historical quotation; Calendar lists conferences and events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission mechanism and accepted file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should be sent electronically to the editors by email at convergence@maa.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles sent in LaTeX, Word, PDF, or HTML formats are welcome, as is a temporary URL for a posted version with all images/applets in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review process and editorial discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions undergo an initial screening by the editors; editors may decline publication without further evaluation or may return a submission for revisions before sending it for peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may appoint additional referees, request minor or major revisions from authors, or commit to a final decision about a manuscript at any point during the review process. 'All refereeing is at least when this is feasible' (editors exercise discretion based on feasibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final submission file format guidance (math notation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For final submission of an accepted article: for an article with very little mathematical notation, submit a Word or any text file; for an article with much mathematical notation, submit a LaTeX file or an html file incorporating MathJax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing math in html/LaTeX submissions, use arrays rather than tables where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation style requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use parenthetical citations and a reference list in the Author-Date form of Chicago Citation Style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Images and applet submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Images should be provided in separate files in png or jpg format; links to any applets should point to GeoGebra's Classroom Resources site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each applet must fit in a window no greater than 700 pixels wide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applet software preference and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Convergence has a definite preference for applets created using the free software GeoGebra, because these applets can be hosted by the MAA account in GeoGebra's Classroom Resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Videos will be hosted by the Convergence YouTube channel. If you cannot produce an applet, search GeoGebra Classroom Resources for similar applets, examine and modify source code, consult an expert on your campus, and if needed contact the editors for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Treasures: image and permission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: High-quality and informative images of a historical mathematical book or object should be provided; images of books typically include the title page and one or more samples of the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain permission from the owner of the book or object to publish the images; check the Index for works already included (earlier editions might be of interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Treasures: text and bibliography requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide approximately 300 words describing the historical significance of the book/object and explaining why the chosen examples are historically or pedagogically interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text must be original to the author (do not copy from Wikipedia, MacTutor, or other sources). Include a bibliography of any sources used and note placements of images within the text. Provide information on the owning repository for acknowledgments and instructions to request permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee sign-up invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential referees should inform editors if they are willing to serve as referees and specify which topics and types of articles they prefer to review.
